scheme_name: "Back Ended Investment Subsidy to Paddy Growers" component of the "Crop Production Technology" scheme
description:
The "Back Ended Investment Subsidy to Paddy Growers" is a significant component of the "Crop Production Technology" scheme initiated by the Government of India.

This scheme was launched in 2014 as part of the National Food Security Mission.

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance the production of paddy through the provision of financial assistance to farmers.

The government aims to increase paddy production by 10 million tonnes by the year 2025.

The scheme specifically targets small and marginal farmers who are engaged in paddy cultivation.

Farmers are provided with a subsidy of 25 percent of the total cost of investment in modern agricultural equipment and technology.

For SC and ST farmers, the subsidy is increased to 30 percent.

The maximum limit for the subsidy is capped at INR 1 lakh per beneficiary.

The assistance is aimed at encouraging the adoption of modern farming techniques.

This includes the use of high-yielding variety seeds and advanced irrigation methods.

The eligibility criteria for this scheme stipulate that applicants must be small and marginal farmers.

Small farmers are defined as those owning less than 2 hectares of land.

Marginal farmers own less than 1 hectare of land.

The annual income of the farmer should not exceed INR 2 lakh.

Farmers must also possess a valid land ownership document.

The application process for the subsidy is straightforward.

Farmers need to approach the nearest Agricultural Department office in their district.

They must fill out the application form provided by the department.

The required documents include proof of land ownership, identity proof, and income certificate.

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the concerned authorities.

The verification process typically takes about 15 to 30 days.

After verification, the subsidy amount is disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account.

The disbursement is usually made within 15 days of approval.

Farmers are encouraged to apply for the subsidy during the kharif season.

The kharif season generally begins in June and ends in October.

The government has allocated INR 500 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2023-2024.

This funding is aimed at supporting approximately 5 lakh farmers across the country.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

State governments are responsible for the on-ground execution of the scheme.

They are tasked with creating awareness among farmers about the benefits of the subsidy.

The Ministry regularly reviews the progress of the scheme.

It conducts periodic assessments to ensure that the objectives are being met.

Farmers are also encouraged to participate in training programs organized by the government.

These programs focus on modern agricultural practices and technologies.

The scheme has seen a significant uptake since its launch.

In the year 2022-2023 alone, over 3 lakh farmers benefited from the subsidy.

The average subsidy amount disbursed per farmer during this period was approximately INR 60,000.

The scheme has contributed to a noticeable increase in paddy yields.

Reports indicate that average yields have increased by 15 to 20 percent in areas where the subsidy was utilized effectively.

Farmers have reported improved income levels due to higher production.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to ensure food security in India.

It aligns with the government's goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The subsidy is not only limited to paddy but also extends to other crops under the Crop Production Technology scheme.

The government is continuously working to improve the scheme based on feedback from farmers.

Regular workshops and seminars are held to gather insights and suggestions.

The scheme is also linked with various digital platforms for better monitoring and transparency.

Farmers can track their application status online through the official government portal.

The government has also introduced a helpline for farmers to address their queries regarding the scheme.

This helpline operates from 9 AM to 6 PM on all working days.

Farmers can call the helpline number 1800 180 1551 for assistance.

The scheme has been instrumental in promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

It encourages the use of eco-friendly technologies and methods.

The government is also exploring partnerships with private sector players to enhance the scheme's reach.

These partnerships aim to provide farmers with access to better technology and resources.

The scheme has received positive feedback from various agricultural organizations.

They have highlighted its role in improving the livelihoods of farmers.

The government is committed to making continuous improvements to the scheme.

This includes increasing the subsidy amount based on inflation and rising costs.

The scheme is expected to evolve in response to changing agricultural needs and challenges.

Overall, the "Back Ended Investment Subsidy to Paddy Growers" component of the "Crop Production Technology" scheme represents a crucial effort by the Indian government to support farmers.

It aims to boost paddy production and improve the economic conditions of small and marginal farmers.

The scheme exemplifies the government's commitment to enhancing agricultural productivity and ensuring food security for the nation.
